%%
%% The abstract is a short summary of the work to be presented in the
%% article.
\begin{abstract}
  The $k$-nearest neighbor (kNN) join is a core operation in modern high-dimensional analytics, widely used in machine learning, vector databases, and data mining. 
While prior work has explored \emph{partially}-dynamic settings where either the query or reference set is updated, efficiently supporting \emph{fully}-dynamic kNN joins remains open. 
%
We study the fully-dynamic kNN join problem on high-dimen\-sional data, where both sets evolve through insertions and deletions. 
We propose \emph{\dualtree}, a dual-index framework that symmetrically maintains an \hdrtree\ on the query set and a \deltatree\ on the reference set, supporting both kNN and reverse kNN (RKNN) searches in a fully dynamic environment. 
To make the pruning efficiency theoretically maximal, we develop a mathematically grounded low-dimensional point-wise pruning strategy that adaptively selects the optimal projection dimension. 
%
Experiments on real high-dimensional datasets show that the \dualtree\ framework equipped with the proposed fine-grained pruning step achieves up to \textbf{2.0}$\times$ speedup over the strongest baseline.
\end{abstract}
\keywords{kNN Join,
High-Dimensional Data,
Dynamic Data}
\maketitle
